source_policy: Original species.json and photo records untouched. Historical flora species treatment recorded only if actually present; FNA separately attributed. County nativity excluded.

references.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
references.note: Printed pages as cited in per-taxon records

references.source: Flora of North America Editorial Committee

morphology.habit: Perennial 5–35 cm, scapiform peduncles, rosette leaves
morphology.leaves: Basal, petioles 0.5–9 cm, blades oblong-oblanceolate 2.5–23 cm, pinnately lobed and spinulose-dentate, hirtellous/stipitate-glandular
morphology.involucres: Turbinate, 14–17 mm; phyllaries 2–4 series, lanceolate to subulate, 3–15 mm
morphology.florets: 25–53 bisexual quasi-radiate two-lipped corollas, pink to lavender-pink, 12–22 mm
morphology.fruits: Cypselae 4–8 mm, glandular and/or hispidulous, pappus 1–17 mm tan or white
morphology.habitat: Juniper woodland, oak woodland, calcareous, sandy clay or gypsiferous soils

open_issues: No matching species account identified in the 1999 regional flora; do not invent a flora page.
FNA describes quasi-radiate/bilabiate florets, not conventional distinct ray and disc florets.

morphology.leaves: Cauline, sessile, oblong-lanceolate to elliptic-oblong blades 2.5–13 cm, sagittate/clasping bases, dentate to denticulate margins, minutely glandular or hairy
morphology.involucres: Turbinate 5–8 mm; 2–3 phyllary series, apices obtuse to acute
morphology.florets: 8–12 pink or purple, corollas 9–20 mm, bilabiate within genus Acourtia
morphology.fruits: Linear-fusiform cypselae 2–6 mm, glandular-puberulent; white pappus 9–12 mm
morphology.habitat: Gravel, caliche or sandy-loamy open desert

open_issues: No matching species account identified in 1999 regional flora.
Species is not a normal ray-and-disc daisy; document quasi-radiate bilabiate heads.

morphology.leaves: Opposite, deltate-ovate to lance-ovate, petioles ca. 1/3 leaf blade length
morphology.heads: Corymbose per broad Eupatorium generic treatment; ray florets absent
morphology.involucres: 4–5 mm, phyllaries mostly similar-sized, scarcely hairy
morphology.fruit: Blackish, 5-ribbed achenes and persistent pappus bristles per generic treatment

morphology.habit: Perennial (30–)50–80(–120) cm, fibrous crown, occasionally rhizomatous
morphology.stems: Ascending to erect, crisped minute puberulence
morphology.leaves: Opposite, petioles (5–)10–30(–50) mm; blades 4–11(–13) × 2.5–8(–9) cm, doubly incised-serrate

open_issues: Eupatorium rugosum is NOT Eupatorium altissimum: the latter is an unrelated distinct entry on p.353.
FNA gives mostly fibrous crowns, sometimes rhizomes; existing record's rhizomatous habit should not be categorical.
Glabrous mature cypselae separate this from hispid A. havanensis.

morphology.leaves: Opposite, deltoid, (2–)3–5(–7) cm long; petioles 3–10(–15) mm
morphology.heads: Corymbose per broad Eupatorium genus treatment
morphology.fruits: Generic Eupatorium: 5-ribbed achenes and pappus bristles

morphology.leaves: Opposite persistent, petioles 3–10(–15) mm; blades (2–)3–5(–8) × 2–5 cm, deltate to broadly ovate or hastate, dentate, nearly hairless, not gland-dotted
morphology.habitat: Limestone bluffs, slopes and stream ledges in oak-juniper woodland

open_issues: FNA's hispid cypselae contrast A. altissima's glabrous ones.
Evergreen leaf persistence FNA documented, not present in older flora account.

morphology.habit: Taprooted broomy annual, 30–40(–60) cm per key; primary stem usually ≤5 mm diam.
morphology.leaves: Alternate sessile; linear (rarely narrowly lanceolate) 0.5–2.5(–3.5) cm × 0.2–1(–2) mm
morphology.heads: Small radiate heads scattered in open panicles
morphology.discs: Functionally staminate, non-fruiting; pappus of long basally united spatulate scales
morphology.fruits: Dark purple-black cypselae 2–3 mm, 4–6 greenish stripes/ribs, long-setulose

morphology.heads: Open paniculiform heads, ray florets 7–12, disc florets 10–21 per genus

open_issues: Diggs explicitly named Gutierrezia amoena as a new combination; FNA re-separates Amphiachyris.
Important source-level ray count disagreement: Diggs generic key 7–15, FNA 7–12. Preserve both.

morphology.habit: Taprooted broomy annual 30–100+ cm; main stem 0.3–1(–2) cm diam.
morphology.leaves: Alternate sessile, narrowly to broadly lanceolate 0.5–6 cm × 0.5–6 mm
morphology.discs: Functionally staminate, not setting fruits, with long joined spatulate pappus scales
morphology.fruits: Purple-black 1.2–2.2 mm cypselae, 7–9 greenish ribs, short-setulose

open_issues: Regional name Gutierrezia, FNA Amphiachyris: same taxon, different genus concept.
FNA lists source distribution without Texas in one rendering; regional flora explicitly says widespread Texas. Flag distribution display mismatch, keep out of BONAP nativity dataset.

morphology.habit: Aromatic woody shrub 40–200(–300) cm; does not root-sprout; trunk relatively thick
morphology.leaves: Persistent, gray-green; blades (0.4–)0.5–3.5 × 0.1–0.7 cm, cuneate and commonly three rounded lobes, densely hairy
morphology.heads: Small discoid heads in upright paniculiform arrays 5–30 × 1–6 cm
morphology.phyllaries: Oblanceolate to widely obovate, densely tomentose
morphology.fruits: Cypselae 1–2 mm hairy or glabrous, glandular; pappus absent per subgenus
morphology.roots: Woody caudex, rhizomes absent per subgenus

open_issues: 1999 flora mentions this species in Artemisia genus overview but does not give a regional species treatment. Do not cite a Diggs species page.
POWO lists native distribution in western North America, omitting Texas; therefore target-county nativity cannot be assumed.
Subspecies boundaries remain disputed in FNA.

morphology.habit: Woody-based perennial herb/small shrub to 1.2 m
morphology.leaves: Sessile or petioles 1–3(–5) mm; blades lanceolate to ovate, usually coriaceous, crenate/serrate
morphology.heads: Elongate racemose/paniculate, with leafy bracts; rays absent
morphology.involucres: Reddish tinged; outer phyllaries much shorter than inner
morphology.fruits: Generic: 10-ribbed cylindrical cypselae; ~30–35 white/nearly white pappus bristles, nonplumose

open_issues: Existing learner says leaves often opposite and densely tomentose beneath, whereas regional flora generic heading says alternate or opposite but species treatment does not resolve arrangement. Preserve, crosscheck FNA.

morphology.habit: Perennial herb 0.4–1.3 m from woody taproot
morphology.leaves: Lanceolate to rhombic-lanceolate, entire to serrate, petioles to 1 cm
morphology.heads: Approximately corymbose with distinctive plumose pappus; ray florets absent
morphology.fruits: 10–20 brownish to white plumose pappus bristles; generic 10-ribbed cypselae
morphology.habitat: Var. corymbulosa/eupatorioides sandy woods; var. texana calcareous prairie
morphology.variety_key: var. corymbulosa: 8.7–15 mm involucres, 14–35 florets; var. eupatorioides: 7–11 mm involucres, 6–15 florets; var. texana: outer/mid phyllaries ≥3/4 as long as inner with twisted/sickle-like tips

open_issues: Historic subspecies/variety delimitations apply only to keyed infraspecific taxa; do not ascribe to unidentified species-level photographs.
